proposals.reason: Section 10 contains three distinct objection-hearing topics: making an objection and triggering a hearing, the Registrar General's path when no objection is delivered, and party/notice rules for a hearing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Objection delivery and required hearing

evidenceText: written statement setting out the reasons for and any grounds and arguments
Registrar General shall hold a hearing to determine the validity of the objection

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10(1) and 10(2) cover how an objection is delivered and the hearing that follows a timely objection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a boundary-confirmation objection is delivered and when it requires the Registrar General to hold a hearing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No-objection confirmation or hearing decision

evidenceText: If no written statement of objection is delivered
confirm the location of the boundary or boundaries
hold a hearing in accordance with this Act and the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 10(3) is a separate decision path for confirmation without a hearing or for holding a hearing when the filed material is not satisfactory.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Registrar General's options when no written objection is delivered by the deadline.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Hearing parties and notice contents

evidenceText: are parties to a hearing held under this section
shall cause a notice of hearing to be given
shall specify the date, time and place of the hearing

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 10(4) through 10(6) identify hearing parties and the content and delivery of hearing notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who is a party to a section 10 hearing and what the notice of hearing must contain.

proposals.reason: The correction provision is one coherent remedy for corrected plans of survey, including authority, notice, boundary limits, filing, cross-reference effect, and notation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corrected boundary-confirmation plan of survey

evidenceText: order that a corrected plan of survey be made
shall not affect the location of a boundary
cause a notation to be made on the plan of survey

proposedGroups.reason: All subsections describe the same corrected-plan workflow and consequences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a corrected boundary-confirmation plan may be ordered, what it cannot change, and how it is filed and noted.

proposals.reason: The target is a short definitions section with six actual defined terms. Splitting is useful only by those target terms, not by context from nearby sections.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Coordinate monument and coordinate survey system definitions

evidenceText: coordinate monument means a brass, bronze or aluminum cap or plate
coordinate survey system means a system established under section 2

proposedGroups.reason: These two definitions describe the coordinate-survey infrastructure used elsewhere in the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a coordinate monument is and what the coordinate survey system means under the Surveys Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corner and legal monument definitions

evidenceText: corner means a point in an intersection of boundaries of land
legal monument means a device planted by a surveyor

proposedGroups.reason: These terms identify boundary points and the physical devices used in survey work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of corner and legal monument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Survey and surveyor definitions

evidenceText: survey means a survey to define the boundaries of land
surveyor means a New Brunswick Land Surveyor

proposedGroups.reason: These two definitions identify the activity and professional actor covered by the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what survey and surveyor mean in the Surveys Act.

proposals.reason: Section 3 is a coherent Director of Surveys topic covering designation, delegation eligibility, and coordinate monument duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Director of Surveys designation and coordinate monument duties

evidenceText: shall designate a surveyor as Director of Surveys
may designate one or more surveyors to perform any of the duties
shall establish and maintain coordinate monuments

proposedGroups.reason: All four subsections concern who may act as Director of Surveys and what the Director does for the coordinate survey system.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Director of Surveys is designated or delegated and the Director's coordinate monument duty.

proposals.reason: Section 8 is one integrated-survey-area plan rule covering surveyor certification, Director acceptance, non-adjudication of title, and application only inside integrated survey areas.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Survey plan certification and acceptance in integrated survey areas

evidenceText: shall not certify to the correctness of the plan unless
Director of Surveys shall not accept it
acceptance does not constitute an adjudication on title
applies to only integrated survey areas

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together as one rule for plans prepared in integrated survey areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the certification, acceptance, title-effect, and application limits for survey plans in integrated survey areas.

proposals.reason: Section 125 is a large regulation-making provision with many distinct planning and development regulation subjects. The groups stay within the regulation-power topics actually listed in the target.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Planning regulation powers for setbacks, sites, signs, extraction, and subdivisions

evidenceText: governing the setting back of buildings and structures
mobile home parks
service stations, gas bars, car washes
public advertising signs and billboards
respecting the subdividing of land

proposedGroups.reason: The opening regulation list groups physical planning controls and subdivision-related regulation powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main planning-control subjects that may be regulated under subsection 125(1).

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development approval and building-work regulation powers

evidenceText: respecting development approvals
building inspection services
building, dimensions, locating or relocating, demolishing, altering

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs focus on development approvals, fees, inspection, and building-work standards.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 125 supports regulations for development approvals, fees, inspections, and building work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Administrative, appeal, delegation, and transitional regulation powers

evidenceText: may delegate a matter to or confer discretion on
appeals
transitional

proposedGroups.reason: The later subsections qualify or support the regulation powers through delegation, appeal, administrative, and transitional machinery.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that section 125 includes supporting powers and limits for how planning and development regulations may operate.

proposals.reason: Section 18 is current despite one repealed subsection. It contains several learnable registration mechanics and legal-effect topics that should be separated by subsection focus.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Instrument receipt, examination, acceptance, and rejection

evidenceText: assign a registration number, date and time
examined
accepted for registration
may refuse to file or register and may reject an instrument

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 18(1) through 18(4) cover the front-end filing/registration workflow and rejection grounds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the registrar's receipt, examination, acceptance, registration, and rejection steps for instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certificates and notices when land or instruments are registered

evidenceText: cancel the certificate of registered ownership
issue to the owner
issue and record under the Registry Act a notice

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections deal with certificates and notices flowing from registration actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what certificate or notice actions accompany registration of land, title, or instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration timing and priority effects

evidenceText: deemed to be registered on the date and at the time
subject to subsection (11)
priority of registration

proposedGroups.reason: The later current subsections address when registration is effective and how priority is determined; subsection 18(8) is repealed and not a study focus.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the timing and priority effects of registration under Land Titles Act section 18.

proposals.reason: Section 19 has separate rules for registration consequences, exceptions and timing for specific instruments, and deed-affidavit forwarding. Repealed subsections 19(8) and 19(9) are not study focuses.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unregistered instrument consequences for purchasers and judgment creditors

evidenceText: deemed fraudulent and void against subsequent purchasers
deemed fraudulent and void as against any bona fide judgment creditor

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(1) and 19(2) state the core legal consequences of non-registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when unregistered instruments are void against purchasers or judgment creditors.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special registration timing rules for leases, auction conveyances, sheriff conveyances, and wills

evidenceText: No lease for a term not exceeding three years
registered within six months
A will registered within six months

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections are distinct timing or exception rules for particular instrument classes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special Registry Act timing and exception rules for leases, official auction conveyances, sheriff conveyances, and wills.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Deed transfer affidavit and forwarding duty

evidenceText: No deed affecting the transfer of real property shall be registered unless accompanied by an affidavit
shall forward the same to the Executive Director of Assessment

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(6) and 19(7) cover the affidavit required with deed registration and what the registrar does with it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the affidavit requirement for real-property deed registration and the registrar's forwarding duty.

proposals.reason: The target is only the citation title for the General Regulation under the Surveys Act. It is useful to recognize but does not justify a memorized StudyUnit.
The target only repeals Regulation 72-160 under the Surveys Act, so it is a repeal-only source with no current substantive rule to memorize.

Regulation 95-166 section 3 contains several concrete boundary-confirmation application topics: the application/form requirement, plan standards, supporting materials, surveyor report contents, and waiver authority.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Boundary confirmation application form and plan standards

evidenceText: application to confirm the location of a boundary
shall be in Form 1
plan of survey required
shall be current and shall conform

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(1) and 3(2) set the application form and current-plan standard.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the required form and plan standards for a boundary-confirmation application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Supporting materials for a boundary confirmation application

evidenceText: shall be accompanied by
field notes and a surveyor's report
copies of all instruments registered
list of the names and mailing addresses

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 3(3) lists the supporting materials that must accompany the application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the field notes, reports, plans, instruments, ownership list, consents, and other documents that may accompany a boundary-confirmation application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surveyor report contents and Registrar General waiver

evidenceText: A surveyor's report
description of the issue to be determined
history of the boundary
Registrar General may waive any of the requirements

proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(4) and 3(5) separately specify surveyor report content and waiver authority.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a boundary-confirmation surveyor's report must contain and when the Registrar General may waive application requirements.

proposals.reason: The target is a regulation-making provision, not a definitions section. Its listed powers are closely related to fees, licence/lease/permit requirements, work requirements, and general implementation under the Underground Storage Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Underground storage regulation-making powers

evidenceText: may make regulations
prescribing the amount of any fee, rental or security
prescribing information that must be contained in an application
terms and conditions and prescribing the form
work requirements

proposedGroups.reason: The section is one compact list of regulation-making powers under the Underground Storage Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the subjects that may be regulated for underground storage fees, applications, licences, leases, construction permits, work requirements, and general implementation.

proposals.source: Energy and Utilities Board Act s. 49.1
proposals.reason: Section 49.1 has one definition needed for the section and one assistance rule. It does not contain land or instrument definition topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulator definition and assistance to the Board

evidenceText: regulator means a regulator as defined in the Financial and Consumer Services Commission Act
may render assistance to the Board without becoming a party
may receive and accept information from the regulator

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections support one topic: who a regulator is and how a regulator may assist the Board in a proceeding.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definition of regulator for section 49.1 and how a regulator may assist the Energy and Utilities Board without becoming a party.

proposals.source: Occupational Health and Safety Act s. 9.1
proposals.reason: OHSA section 9.1 is a substantive duties provision. It should not be reference-only merely because it mentions regulations; the target imposes explicit supervisor duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General supervisor health and safety duties

evidenceText: Every supervisor shall
take every reasonable precaution
comply with this Act, the regulations and any order
ensure that the employees under the supervisor's supervision and direction comply
co-operate with

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 9.1(1) lists the general statutory duties of supervisors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the general OHSA duties every supervisor owes for employee health and safety, compliance, and cooperation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Supervisor hazard, information, and instruction duties

evidenceText: acquaint the employees
with any hazard
provide the information
provide the instruction

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 9.1(2) adds specific duties to acquaint employees with hazards and provide necessary information and instruction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the supervisor's specific hazard-warning, information, and instruction duties.

proposals.reason: Section 5 is not regulation-making authority; it lists who may hold a conservation easement, with one repealed paragraph and several current holder categories.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Who may hold a conservation easement

evidenceText: Any of the following may hold a conservation easement
Crown in right of the Province
Crown in right of Canada
a local government
a non-profit corporation
any person, body or group or class of persons

proposedGroups.reason: The provision is a compact list of eligible conservation easement holders, so one StudyUnit is enough.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the public, non-profit, and prescribed private categories that may hold a conservation easement.

proposals.reason: Section 39.1 is a focused permit rule for access to highways that are not controlled access highways, with a prohibition/permit requirement and a safety-standard basis for granting a permit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Permit for access to non-controlled-access highway

evidenceText: No person shall construct, use or permit the use
without obtaining a permit from the Minister
Minister may grant an application
would not be inconsistent with such safety standards

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections describe one access-permit rule and the Minister's safety-standard approval condition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a permit is required for access to a highway that is not controlled access and the basis on which the Minister may grant it.

proposals.reason: Section 27 is a focused mandatory reporting provision for specified health professionals. The reference to regulations describes how reports are made and does not make the section reference-only.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Professional reporting duty for notifiable disease, injury risk, or notifiable event

evidenceText: shall report to a medical officer of health
reasonable grounds to believe
has or may have a notifiable disease
has or may be affected by an injury or risk factor
has suffered a notifiable event
shall be made in accordance with the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections state who must report, the triggering beliefs, and the required manner of reporting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which professionals must report under Public Health Act section 27, what triggers the report, and that the report is made according to the regulations.

proposals.reason: Section 17.11 is one electronic filing topic for digitally scanned images, including when image submission is allowed, required format/technology, and identity or authorization evidence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Digitally scanned image filing or registration of instruments

evidenceText: may be filed or registered by submitting a digitally scanned image
shall be in a format that has been approved by the Registrar General
shall be submitted using the technology put in place by Service New Brunswick
shall provide to the registrar evidence of his or her identity or authorization

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together as one rule for filing or registering instruments by digitally scanned image.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when Land Titles Act instruments may be submitted as digitally scanned images and what format, technology, and identity evidence are required.

proposals.reason: Section 30 is one coherent Personal Property Registry notice rule for household-goods orders, including registration, amendment, notice effect, and exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Personal Property Registry notice of household-goods order

evidenceText: may register a notice of the order in the Personal Property Registry
may be renewed, discharged or otherwise amended
shall be deemed to be notice of the order and its terms
does not apply to

proposedGroups.reason: All subsections describe the same registered-notice mechanism and its exceptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a notice of a household-goods order is registered, amended, and treated as notice, plus the serial-number and consumer-goods exceptions.

proposals.reason: Section 7 is one evidentiary compellability rule: a witness cannot refuse to answer because of self-incrimination risk, but the compelled evidence has limited later use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compelled answers and limited later use in provincial proceedings

evidenceText: no person shall be excused from answering any question
may tend to render him liable to a prosecution, penalty or forfeiture
no evidence so given shall be used or receivable in evidence
other than a prosecution for perjury

proposedGroups.reason: The section states one rule and one protection for compelled answers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a witness must answer despite possible provincial prosecution or penalty exposure, and that the answer is generally not usable later except for perjury.

proposals.reason: Registry Act section 23 has related but distinct will-registration paths: extra-provincial court copies/probate materials, proof when probate has not been granted, and notarial wills.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registering extra-provincial court will materials affecting land

evidenceText: where a will affecting land in this Province
is deposited in any court out of this Province
certified copy thereof, the probate of such will
may be registered in the registry office

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 23(1) covers registration of certified copies, probate, letters, or exemplifications from an extra-provincial court.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what extra-provincial court will materials may be registered in New Brunswick and their effect when registered.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affidavits required when extra-provincial will probate is absent

evidenceText: has not been granted probate
affidavit sworn by one of the witnesses
affidavit of the death of the testator

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 23(2) adds a separate proof requirement when probate has not been granted.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the affidavits required to register an extra-provincial will when probate has not been granted.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of Quebec or South Africa notarial wills

evidenceText: notarial will under the laws of the Province of Quebec or of South Africa
notarial certified copy
valid and subsisting will

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 23(3) is a distinct path for notarial wills from Quebec or South Africa.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special registration rule for Quebec or South Africa notarial wills affecting land in New Brunswick.

proposals.reason: Aquaculture Act section 19 is a short but substantive rent duty for lease holders, with the amount fixed by regulation or by the Registrar when no regulation applies.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aquaculture lease-holder rent amount

evidenceText: A lease holder shall pay rent
in an amount fixed by the regulations
when there is no applicable regulation, at a rent fixed by the Registrar

proposedGroups.reason: The single provision states one clear rent obligation and fallback amount-setting rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who pays aquaculture lease rent and how the rent amount is fixed.

proposals.source: Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors Bylaws s. 4.2.2
proposals.reason: Bylaw section 4.2.2 is one procedural approval rule for the amount of a special levy: Council determines it and voting members approve it at an annual or special meeting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special levy amount determination and member approval

evidenceText: amount of the special levy shall be determined by the Council
approved at either the annual general meeting or a special meeting
by a vote of the voting members present

proposedGroups.reason: The provision is a compact rule for determining and approving a special levy amount.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the amount of an ANBLS special levy is determined and approved.

proposals.source:
Agricultural Land Protection
and Development Act s. 10
proposals.reason: The target is a genuine repeal-only provision for registered agricultural land and contains no operative current rule for StudyUnit authoring.
